name: safety-projection-visual
description: Visual verification of safety and projection systems: safety zone evacuation before blast, blast projection trajectories based on overcharge/stemming/free face/sequence, buildings/vehicles in projection path, and post-blast damage assessment.

steps.description: #553: switched from `campaign start level:dusty_hollow` -- dusty_hollow's 96x40x96 grid put a manually-bought vehicle's grid-centre spawn far enough from the drill site to matter, and campaign start has no staffed:true equivalent anyway. staffed:true (a driller with blasting + drill_rig licence, plus an unmanned drill_rig, hired/purchased for free) is what #553's automatic drill dispatch needs to ever land an ordered hole. Cash bumped to $250,000 for headroom through the drilling wait (no income anywhere in this file) on top of the freight_warehouse/software-tier spend already here.

steps.command: zone clear x1:5 y1:5 x2:35 y2:35

interaction.command: zone clear x1:5 y1:5 x2:35 y2:35

steps.description: Left unmarked, confirmed not equivalent (not merely unverified): Fire.ts's Sound the Horn button (`[data-action="sound-horn"]`) sends `zone clear` using `currentZone = computeDangerZone(state.drillHoles, BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M)` -- a rectangle derived from the live drill plan, never a player-typed one. At this point in the file state.drillHoles is empty (the file's only drill_plan step runs later), so computeDangerZone returns null, this.currentZone is null, and the horn button is disabled outright (occupants defaults to [] when zone is null, and hornBtn.disabled = occupants.length === 0) -- soundHorn() itself also no-ops on a null zone (`if (!zone) return;`). A player cannot produce this command by clicking here: not a different rectangle, but a control that doesn't work yet at this point in the scenario. (Later in the file, once the 4x4/spacing:3 grid at (20,20) exists, computeDangerZone's own padding would still produce (5,5,44,44), not this step's literal (5,5,35,35) -- so even a same-moment click would diverge from this explicit rectangle.)

expect.note: no state field exposes zone bounds/status -- proven instead by the zone status observe step's own text output

steps.description: #553 crew-walkout fix (issue #586 CI): the staffed driller working this 4x4=16-hole pattern unattended for the hundreds of real ticks drilling now takes runs well-being down far enough that WORKER REVOLT fires right as the last hole lands (razor-thin, confirmed sandbox-measured on this exact seed) -- its full-screen game-over overlay then blocks every subsequent panel click, exactly the `clickSelector "#bs-blast-panel [data-step=\"2\"]" failed: element is covered by div` CI failure. Adding a second working drill_rig was tried first and rejected: it changes hole-completion ORDER (two drillers interleave which hole lands when), and this file's blast turned out to be order-sensitive -- sequence auto's V-pattern delay assignment produced a measurably different fragment count and, worse, destroyed the freight_warehouse this file's whole safety-zone premise depends on surviving (sandbox-confirmed: identical 1114 cleared voxels either way, but a different exact voxel set). Two idle, unrigged relief hires instead (this employee and the one below) leave the sole driller's own drilling completely unchanged -- same order, same timing, same blast outcome, byte-for-byte (sandbox-confirmed: 2230 fragments and the warehouse at full HP, identical to the pre-fix file) -- while their fresh, untouched needs pull the roster's average morale (and therefore well-being, ScoreManager.ts) up just enough that the 120-tick WORKER REVOLT countdown never matures before tick 400. Employee #6 (staffed:true's own roster already occupies ids 1-5). #553-followup: the preceding step (`build freight_warehouse`) leaves the build panel active (ToolRail's click handler is a togglePanel toggle, UIManager.ts:450), not employees -- added the toolbar employees-panel click as the first action here so the driller row is actually visible before waitForSelector/clickSelector reach it.
#553 crew-walkout fix: employee #7, the second idle relief hire -- see the step above for why. Deliberately left unrigged and unskilled, same as employee #6.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:4 cols:4 spacing:3 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: Corrected from the original rows:3 cols:3 spacing:5 (which command mode ran literally, producing 9 holes): the click drags the (20,20)-(30,30) rectangle at the Drill panel's own default spacing (DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3), computing cols/rows as round(size/spacing)+1 = 4x4 = 16 holes for that same rectangle -- the command and the click were silently testing two different grids, the same class of bug already fixed in nav-cell-types-visual.json. Caught by adding expect.equals.holeCount; fixed by describing what the click actually produces. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: spacing deliberately left at the default 3m rather than tightened like most other files' 9-16-hole grids -- a sandbox-measured trial at 2m produced a drastically more violent CATASTROPHIC blast (1259 affected voxels vs. 3m's much smaller footprint) that destroyed the freight_warehouse this file's own safety-zone premise depends on surviving. Cash bumped further ($250,000) to cover the longer drilling wait at the unmodified 3m spacing instead.

#553: drain the ordered plan in bounded 50-tick chunks -- each chunk is followed by `event choose 0` since a `tick` command stops dead the instant a timer event fires mid-block (events.ts). Sandbox-measured landing at tick 300 (6 chunks) for this 16-hole grid with the staffed roster's single driller (#554-followup, issue #586 CI: the file previously ran 8 chunks/400 ticks -- a direct trace showed the extra 2 chunks were dead padding past the point all 16 holes had already landed, trimmed below).

Sixth and final chunk — all 16 holes should have landed by now. Two further chunks (300->400 ticks) were dropped here (#554-followup, issue #586 CI): a direct trace showed all 16 holes already landed by tick 300 (end of this chunk) with orderedHoleCount already 0, so the extra 100 ticks the file used to spend past that point were pure padding -- and exactly that padding pushed wellBeing's already-zero streak (pinned at 0 since ~tick 300, REVOLT_TICKS=120, WorkerRevolt.ts) past the revolt threshold during the charge-order wait_until step below, ending the level via worker_revolt before the auto-sequence click ever got a chance to run as real, clickable UI -- the interaction-mode `[data-step="3"]` click that surfaced the real CI failure needs the sequence panel to still be reachable, which a worker_revolt's full-viewport LevelEndScreen overlay permanently prevents. Trimming the dead padding keeps the level alive long enough for charge/sequence/blast to run as genuine player interaction, same fix and same reasoning as core-loop-visual.json's identical dead-padding-before-revolt finding.

role: player (issue #515): the Charge step's amount/stemming steppers and product-card explosive selector are real controls — this reaches the declared explosive/amount/stemming via clicks instead of Charge All using whatever the panel's fields already showed. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): stemming raised 1.0 m -> 1.8 m, the fix for the freight_warehouse dying in interaction mode while command mode kept it alive. Root cause is flyrock, not the crater: a building is destroyed either by a cleared voxel landing inside its footprint (BlastExecution.ts step 5b) or by a thrown fragment coming to rest within HIT_RADIUS=2.0 m of its centre with >=500 J (processProjections, Damage.ts, called from the blast command). At 1.0 m stemming on 6 m holes the charge vents to the surface and throws 444 projections up to ~52 m across a 64x64 m site, so *every* tile on the map is inside flyrock range and warehouse survival is a lottery on where those 444 land. What decides that is the auto-sequence delay layout, which keys off state.drillHoles' array ORDER, and interaction mode fills that array in real-time drill-completion order rather than command mode's fixed plan order. Sandbox-measured over 64 shuffled completion orders on this exact setup: at amount:8 stemming:1 the warehouse survives 42/64 (closest projection landed 0.2 m from its centre, peak damage 9345 vs 150 HP); at amount:8 stemming:1.8 it survives 64/64, closest landing 3.8 m -- nearly 2x the 2.0 m hit radius, with no hit recorded at all. Rejected alternatives, both sandbox-measured: (a) moving the warehouse further out does nothing, because flyrock at 1.0 m stemming is sprayed over the whole site -- (38,25) 11/24, (40,25) 11/24, (42,25) 11/24, (45,25) 12/24, i.e. still a coin flip 16 tiles away, and at 1.8 m stemming (45,25) is actually *worse* (29/32) than (35,25) (64/64); (b) cutting the charge to 6 kg also holds, but throws away the overcharge this file exists to visualise (77 projections vs 147). Stemming is the physically right knob anyway -- flyrock is what an under-stemmed hole produces, and 1.0 m of stemming on a 6 m hole is barely a sixth of the column. The blast stays CATASTROPHIC and gets *bigger*, not tamer: confining it puts more energy into the rock (1247 cleared voxels vs 1114), it still throws 147 projections ~51 m for the projection preview to draw, and ecology/nuisance still drop. Panel clicks follow the value: DEFAULT_STEMMING_M=2 with 0.2 m per click (Charge.ts), so one decrement now instead of five.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

Sequence's delay-step stepper now carries data-field="delay-step" (Sequence.ts, matching the drill grid tool's ParamStrip.ts convention) so a click can target it unambiguously -- the Charge step's amount/stemming steppers use the same unscoped .bsx-stepper markup and stayed indistinguishable without it. 3 decrement clicks: 25ms default -> 20 -> 15 -> 10 (DELAY_STEP_INCREMENT=5ms, Sequence.ts).
preview projections requires software tier 3+ (default tier is 0) — unlock sequentially so the projection preview actually computes instead of printing a lock message

expect.note: Finding #36: buy_software used to leave state.finances.cash diverged from this flat field by the sum of every tier cost, fixed at the root. #553-followup: dropped the hardcoded `equals: {cash: 60430}` -- adding the employees-panel toolbar click to the Employee #6 hire step above (see that step's own note) is interaction-mode-only (command mode's own `employee hire role:driller` string is untouched), and processFrame ticks off the render loop's own wall clock while `time resume` is in effect (GameLoop.ts): one extra CDP round-trip before this checkpoint means interaction mode now accrues different payroll than command mode's fully tick-command-driven, unaffected 60430 (sandbox-measured: interaction mode lands on 60684 here, deterministic for a given host load, but not equal to command mode's own value). `decreased` alone still proves the tier-3 purchase actually spent cash in both modes, matching tier:1/tier:2's own steps above, which never asserted an exact figure to begin with.

a preview is read-only -- no cash or hole/charge/sequence count moves. #553-followup: switched the read-only proof from an exact cash figure to chargedCount/sequencedCount -- cash is real-time-tick-sensitive in interaction mode (see buy_software tier:3's own note above) and no longer has a single value both modes agree on, while charge/sequence counts don't decay with elapsed ticks the way cash does, so they hold in both modes regardless of host timing.

buildingCount stays 1 -- the freight_warehouse the safety-zone/projection setup is built around survives the blast unscathed (confirmed via direct trace: HP 150/150 unchanged), which is this file's own premise about the safety zone doing its job. #553-followup (issue #586 CI): this used to hold in command mode and fail in interaction mode; it now holds in both because the charge step's stemming went 1.0 m -> 1.8 m, which drops flyrock from 444 projections to 147 and moves the closest landing from 0.2 m to 3.8 m of the warehouse centre against a 2.0 m hit radius (Damage.ts HIT_RADIUS) -- survival measured 64/64 over shuffled drill-completion orders instead of 42/64. Full measurement and the rejected alternatives are in the charge step's own description. Deliberately NOT weakened to a note-only field: proving the building survives is what this file is for.
